# ControlButton

A compact, icon-only button for controlling an interactive container — a media player, carousel, lightbox, or modal. Reach for it when the icon alone carries the action: play/pause, next/previous, mute, expand, close.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.4.3`, `1.4.11`, `2.1.1`, `2.4.7`, `2.5.8`, `4.1.2`

- Renders a native <button>, or an <a> when it navigates — never a div with a click handler.
- The label is the accessible name; an icon-only button needs an aria-label.
- Focus is visible on the control itself (2.4.7) and the target is at least 24x24 (2.5.8).
- Disabled is conveyed to assistive tech, not by colour alone (1.4.1).
- Give every instance an accessible name. It shows only an icon, so set an aria-label that states the action ("Play", "Next slide", "Close"). WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — every control exposes a name and role to assistive tech.
- It's a real button. Implement as a <button> so it's reachable by keyboard: Tab moves to it, Enter and Space activate it. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard — all functionality works without a mouse.
- The focus state isn't decoration. The focus variant's ring must ship in code so keyboard users can see where they are. WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible.
- Watch contrast on media. Over photo or video the glyph can wash out — keep it on the component's scrim so it holds at least 3:1 against the background. WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.
- Keep the target big enough. Present at least a 24x24px pointer target (44x44 is better on touch). WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
- disabled is communicated, not just dimmed. Remove it from the tab order and expose the disabled state to assistive tech.
